capitals.name: Sukhumi
capitals.note: Capital and largest city; held by Georgian forces until 27 September 1993.

correction.text: Abkhazia without the Upper Kodori Valley, which 'remained under Georgian control (until 2008)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1992-2008, from the declaration of independence; the Abkhaz forces 'overran the whole territory of Abkhazia' by 30 September 1993 except the upper Kodori Valley. Natural Earth's Abkhazia admin-1 resolves to 8,346 km2 against the infobox 8,665 km2 (ratio 0.96); the Kodori valley is a 25 km circle (a reading: the page gives no boundary).

correction.text: the whole of Abkhazia, 8,665 km2, with the Upper Kodori Valley after August 2008

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 2009-2024 (2008 for the Kodori gain is in the ledger). Infobox 8,664.59 km2; the admin-1 resolves to 8,346 km2 (0.96). Recognised by Russia (26 August 2008), Venezuela, Nicaragua and Syria; the Gali District is inside the shape.

ledger.note: 23 July 1992: Abkhazia declares independence from Georgia. Infobox 'Abkhazian declaration of independence: 23 July 1992' (sovereignty declaration 25 August 1990; act of state independence 12 October 1999); the page says Georgia's military council restored the 1921 constitution on 21 February 1992. [Reviewer eu-19-x, 2026-10-31: counterpart and predecessor set to georgia: the georgian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier ends in April 1991 (independence of the Republic of Georgia), before this July 1992 declaration; georgia is the slug the other events of this dossier use.]

region.text: Abkhazia, fought over from Gagra to Sukhumi

ledger.note: 14 August 1992: Georgian forces enter Abkhazia and the war begins. 'On August 14, the National Guard of Georgia entered Abkhazia'; a ceasefire on 3 September obliged Georgian forces to leave Gagra, which Abkhaz forces took on 2 October 1992.

region.text: Abkhazia except the Upper Kodori Valley

ledger.note: 27 September 1993: Sukhumi falls and the Abkhaz take the land. 'After a fierce battle, Sukhumi fell on 27 September'; Abkhaz forces 'overran the whole territory of Abkhazia' except 'the upper Kodori Valley remained in Georgian hands' (about 250,000 Georgians expelled in 1992-1993, Abkhazia page).

1994: the ceasefire holds and the front ends. The page mentions a '1994 ceasefire agreement' and a CIS peacekeeping force without a day (the war page ends the war on 30 September 1993; the Moscow ceasefire of 14 May 1994 is not on either page).

August 2008: Abkhaz and Russian forces take the Upper Kodori Valley. The Upper Kodori Gorge 'remained under Georgian control (until 2008)'; the August 2008 war 'escalated into a full-scale war between the Russian Federation and the Republic of Georgia' and Russia recognised Abkhazia on 26 August 2008.

wars.name: War in Abkhazia (1992-1993)
wars.outcome: Georgian forces entered on 14 August 1992; Gagra fell on 2 October 1992; a Russian-brokered ceasefire of 27 July 1993 was broken and Sukhumi fell on 27 September 1993; the Abkhaz held all Abkhazia except the Upper Kodori Valley and Georgians were expelled.

wars.name: Russo-Georgian War (Abkhaz front)
wars.outcome: In August 2008 Abkhaz and Russian forces took the Upper Kodori Valley from Georgia; Russia recognised Abkhazia on 26 August 2008.
wars.note: The war page itself was not opened; the Abkhazia page gives the year, the escalation and the recognition date.

certainty.note: The old Abkhaz ASSR boundary and the line along the Inguri; the Kodori valley edge is approximate.

notes: No Cliopatria row for the modern republic (Cliopatria's 'Georgia' row has 1992 and 2024 shapes, handled by eu-19-b, which cover Abkhazia as Georgian land). The Abkhazia dossier is drawn as separatist state; the Georgia dossier should show the contest and Georgian loss with counterpart republic-of-abkhazia (and republic-of-south-ossetia). Upper Kodori Valley is a 25 km circle at 41.9 E, 43.05 N (approximate, no named region). Russia's recognition (26 August 2008) and Abkhazia's client status towards the Russian Federation are not drawn: the russian-federation dossier may add vassal_start for republic-of-abkhazia. Gali District is Georgian-populated and inside the shape. Not opened: the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict page, the 1994 Moscow agreement, the 1999 independence act. wikidata null.
